agreement.text:
What Sanad is
Sanad is an AI assistant that Dr Dr. Samir Test uses to follow the plan made at your visit. Linking your Telegram account needs your consent and your doctor's confirmation that the account is really yours.

What we process, and why
Your messages, voice notes, photos, account details and your doctor's plan. We use them only to explain your plan, remind you, and collect follow-up for your doctor.

Who handles your data
- Telegram carries the messages between you and Sanad.
- Amazon Web Services stores your data on servers in the United States, and Amazon's AI models read your messages.
- Google Gemini reads your voice notes and photos.
Messages with the bot are not end-to-end encrypted clinical communication.

How often we contact you
Routine follow-up is at most one reminder message a day, outside your quiet hours (22:00 to 08:00, Africa/Cairo). Reminders at fixed times, or during your quiet hours, need your separate agreement.

What Sanad cannot do
Sanad can make mistakes. It does not diagnose, prescribe or change your doctor's instructions. It is not an emergency service and does not promise a time for your doctor to reply. In an emergency, go to the nearest emergency department or call 123 for an ambulance.

Your choices
You can say no now. You can pause reminders at any time. You can withdraw your consent completely by contacting the clinic: Synthetic Demo Clinic front desk, demonstration only. Your doctor can also remove you from Sanad. Withdrawing does not change your treatment.

How long we keep your data
While you are linked to your doctor, we keep your data to follow your plan. If you withdraw or your doctor removes you, Sanad stops contacting you straight away. Your messages, voice notes and photos are deleted within 30 days. The medical record your doctor accepted is kept for as long as your doctor is required to keep medical records, then deleted. Deleted data can remain in our encrypted backups for up to 35 more days before it is gone.

Your record of agreement
We keep a record that you agreed and which version of these terms you saw.
